## Cybersecurity Industry Hiring Analysis — Executive Summary
### Week of March 20, 2026

This week's analysis tracked 209 cybersecurity and adjacent technology companies, with successful job listing data retrieved from 15 firms. The remaining 194 companies could not be assessed due to a fundamental scraper limitation: the majority of enterprise career pages rely on JavaScript-rendered frameworks that our automated tooling cannot currently process. As a result, the absence of job data for those companies should not be interpreted as evidence of hiring freezes or reduced headcount activity — actual hiring status for those organizations remains unknown and would require manual review or API-level career data integration to assess accurately. All strategic insights and trend analysis below are drawn exclusively from the 15 companies where reliable data was collected.

Among the companies with retrievable data, the dominant theme this week is the rapid institutionalization of AI-native security as a distinct engineering and product discipline — not merely a feature layer, but a foundational architectural shift. Okta's aggressive buildout around Agentic AI and Non-Human Identity (NHI), Wiz's investment in a dedicated Threat & AI Research team alongside a new AI-native DAST capability, and Cato Networks' post-acquisition expansion of a full AI Security business unit (following their Aim Security acquisition) all signal that the industry's leading players are treating AI security as a standalone, revenue-generating product category rather than an extension of existing platforms. Similarly, Abnormal Security's formal "AI Transformation" initiative — standing up a cross-functional team to accelerate ML-to-production pipelines — and Orca Security's dedicated AI Platform team reflect a broader pattern of security vendors rebuilding their core detection and risk prioritization engines around ML infrastructure. Elastic's investment in vector search and serverless security analytics, combined with Datadog's bold bet on training proprietary foundation models through its new DAIR research organization, further illustrates that the competitive frontier is shifting toward organizations that own their AI stack rather than those that merely integrate third-party models. Frontegg's emergence as a potential infrastructure middleware player for the AI agent economy — with dedicated MCP Gateway development and a new "Agen" product line — is an early but notable signal worth monitoring, as protocol-level bets of this kind often foreshadow broader ecosystem consolidation.

From a hiring volume and organizational health standpoint, Datadog (456 open positions), Okta (370), Elastic Security (220), Rubrik (204), and Wiz (187) represent the most active hiring organizations this week, each carrying health scores of 7–8 out of 10 with growing trend indicators. Rubrik's pivot into Identity Resilience as a standalone product line — with dedicated sales, engineering, and product leadership — and its investment in the "Zero Labs" AI threat research brand suggest the company is actively repositioning beyond its data protection roots. Cato Networks (161 open positions) and Abnormal Security (111) round out the high-activity tier. At the other end of the spectrum, Sonrai Security, Frontegg, Archer (via Broadcom), ServiceNow GRC, and Indigo each showed only 1–2 retrievable listings; notably, the Archer data appears to reflect a misattributed scrape result from an unrelated veterinary entity, rendering those signals unreliable. Salary benchmarking remains unavailable this cycle as the majority of active listings did not include compensation ranges, limiting our ability to assess compensation trends or geographic labor market signals for this reporting period.
